newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fruit, veges lead NZ Food prices higher in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Fruit, veges lead NZ Food prices higher in Feb.

text.p: Food prices in February went up by 0.2 percent, with the prices for fruit and vegetables leading the rise, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
The February increase follows a rise of 0.6 percent in January and a fall of 0.7 percent in December. The Food Price Index is now 2.7 percent higher than in February 1996.
"An increase in the price of tomatoes was the main factor in an overall rise of 3.1 percent for fruit and vegetables," SNZ said.
"There were more price increases recorded for vegetables than fruit but of the fruit, apples and bananas recorded the largest price increases."
Grocery prices overall showed a decrease of 0.2 percent in February. When compared to February 1996, grocery prices in February 1997 are 2.3 percent higher.
Prices of meat, fish and poultry fell by 0.9 percent in February.
Restaurant meals and ready-to-eat food recorded an increase of 0.3 percent in February and are now 2.2 percent higher than in February 1996.

Prices in the North Island rose by 0.4 percent mainly due to increases in fruit and vegetable prices. In the South Island, prices declined by 0.3 percent mainly due to a fall in the price of meat, fish and poultry, SNZ said.
